Section 1: Executive Summary & Operating Reality

JD.com, Inc. (JD) is navigating a complex macroeconomic transition in China's domestic e-commerce landscape, characterized by intense price competition, shifting consumer preferences, and category-specific headwinds. Under the active leadership of Chief Executive Officer Ms. Sandy Ran Xu and Chief Financial Officer Mr. Ian Su Shan, the company’s Q2 2026 financial results represent a definitive turning point in its profitability trajectory. While total net revenues experienced a slight contraction of 2.9% year-over-year to RMB 346.4 billion (US$151.1 billion)—primarily driven by a high comparison base and component price inflation in the electronics and home appliances categories—the business achieved a massive profit inflection. Non-GAAP net income surged 20.8% year-over-year to RMB 8.93 billion (US$1.3 billion), demonstrating the structural resilience of JD's supply chain-driven model and an intentional shift from low-margin volume acquisition to high-quality user monetization.

The operational turnaround is anchored by two primary engines: the record-high profitability of its core JD Retail segment and a dramatic narrowing of losses in its New Businesses. JD Retail's gross margin expanded by 130 basis points year-over-year to a record 18.5% for a peak promotional quarter, marking the 17th consecutive quarter of year-over-year gross margin expansion. This was supported by a favorable revenue mix as high-margin marketplace and marketing revenues rose 8.3% (driven by robust advertising demand) and net service revenues grew 6.8% to RMB 79.3 billion. Concurrently, JD Logistics continued its strong external expansion, with revenues growing 24.3% year-over-year to RMB 68.1 billion, while operating losses in New Businesses narrowed significantly, led by a >50% year-over-year reduction in JD Food Delivery losses through optimized unit economics and reduced subsidies.

From a capital allocation and balance sheet perspective, JD.com remains an absolute fortress. The company generated a stellar RMB 37.72 billion (US$5.56 billion) in operating cash flow for the quarter, driving trailing 12-month free cash flow to RMB 31.4 billion—a dramatic recovery from RMB 10.1 billion in the prior-year period, fueled by disciplined working capital management and normalized trade-in cash outflows. Backed by a massive cash pile of RMB 235.1 billion (US$34.6 billion) in cash, restricted cash, and short-term investments, management has aggressively returned capital to shareholders. In the first half of 2026, JD.com repurchased approximately 69.9 million Class A ordinary shares (equivalent to 34.9 million ADSs) for US$1.0 billion, retiring roughly 2.5% of its outstanding share count. This capital-light compounding profile, combined with a deeply discounted valuation, provides an exceptional margin of safety as the company prepares for top-line growth to normalize and accelerate in the second half of 2026.

Sandy Xu, Chief Executive Officer of JD.com, on the Profitability Inflection:
“Q2 marked a definitive turning point for our profitability trajectory. Our non-GAAP net income attributable to ordinary shareholders surged by 21% year-on-year to RMB 8.9 billion, driven by both JD Retail's healthy margin expansion and JD Food Delivery's loss reduction... These results underscore the resilience of our supply chain-driven business model and our team's focus on operational efficiency—strengths that we believe will continue to set us apart as we capture future growth opportunities.”

Ian Su Shan, Chief Financial Officer of JD.com, on Capital Return & Margin Outlook:
“We delivered solid profitability in the second quarter despite moderating top-line momentum. JD Retail's operating margin hit a record high for peak promotional seasons. This performance was driven by margin improvement in certain key categories, as well as a favorable revenue mix as high-margin marketplace and marketing revenues continued to outperform... Backed by our solid financial performance, we repurchased approximately 2.5% of our ordinary shares outstanding in the first half of the year, underscoring our commitment to shareholder returns.”

Section 2: Business Model Reality, Unit Economics & Competitive Moat

JD.com, Inc. (JD) operates a highly resilient, hybrid e-commerce and supply chain model that distinguishes it from pure-play marketplace competitors. The company's Q2 2026 financial results represent a definitive turning point in profitability, demonstrating that its asset-heavy, supply chain-first strategy can deliver robust bottom-line expansion even in a low-growth, highly competitive macroeconomic environment.

Strategic Note on Segment Reclassification: The sharp decline in New Businesses revenue (-47.6%) and corresponding surge in JD Logistics revenue (+24.3%) was primarily driven by the strategic transfer of on-demand delivery services (including JD Food Delivery's fulfillment arm) from New Businesses to JD Logistics, effective January 2026. This integration optimized crowdsourced delivery capabilities and converted internal cost centers into high-margin external merchant service revenues.

How JD.com Makes Money, Customer Switching Costs & Pricing Power

1. Revenue Generation Mechanics

JD.com employs a dual-engine monetization model:

  • First-Party (1P) Direct Sales (80.3% of Retail Revenue): JD acts as a traditional merchant, purchasing inventory directly from brands (especially electronics, home appliances, and fast-moving consumer goods). JD takes inventory risk but captures the spread between wholesale procurement and retail pricing. This model guarantees product authenticity and underpins the company's reputation for quality.
  • Third-Party (3P) Marketplace & Services (19.7% of Retail Revenue): JD operates an open platform for external merchants. It monetizes this traffic through transaction commissions, platform usage fees, and high-margin digital advertising/marketing services (which grew 8.3% YoY in Q2 2026).
  • Integrated Supply Chain Services: JD Logistics (JDL) charges external merchants and corporate clients for warehousing, freight, cold-chain transport, and last-mile delivery. External customers now contribute over 60% of JDL's total revenue, proving its viability as a standalone commercial network.

2. Customer Switching Costs

For retail consumers, pure digital switching costs are low; they can easily toggle between JD, Taobao, and Pinduoduo. However, JD has built a powerful, asymmetric convenience and trust switching cost. Consumers who prioritize guaranteed product authenticity (zero tolerance for counterfeits) and ultra-fast, predictable delivery (same-day or next-day via JDL's "211" program) face a severe drop-off in service utility if they migrate to asset-light platforms. For enterprise merchants, switching costs are high and structural; integrating their ERP systems, inventory forecasting, and physical warehousing with JD's logistics network binds them operationally to JD's ecosystem.

3. Evidence of Pricing Power

JD's pricing power does not manifest as premium retail markups—which are unviable in China's current "consumption downgrading" climate—but rather as upstream monopsony power and service monetization resilience. Due to its massive scale as China's largest retailer by revenue, JD dictates procurement terms to electronics and home appliance manufacturers. This upstream leverage allowed JD Retail to expand its gross margin by 1.3 percentage points YoY to 18.5% in Q2 2026, marking its 17th consecutive quarter of year-over-year gross margin expansion despite intense domestic price wars.

Structural Secular Tailwinds vs. Competitive Disruption Threats

Structural Secular Tailwinds

  • National Trade-In Subsidies: China's state-sponsored consumer goods trade-in program for green home appliances and energy-efficient electronics directly favors JD's core, high-AOV (Average Order Value) categories, driving a projected demand recovery in H2 2026.
  • Autonomous Fulfillment Scale: JD Logistics has deployed thousands of unmanned delivery vehicles across 20+ provinces, launching night-time autonomous routes in Shenzhen. This technology structurally lowers last-mile fulfillment costs, which are JD's largest operational overhead.
  • Upmarket Service Premiumization: As brands seek to bypass price wars, premium houses (e.g., Chanel's beauty flagship launch in May 2026) and warehouse clubs (e.g., Costco's exclusive China e-commerce partnership in July 2026) are selecting JD as their exclusive partner due to its trusted cold-chain and white-glove delivery capabilities.

Competitive Disruption & Substitution Threats

  • Social Commerce Disintermediation: Live-streaming platforms like Douyin and social directories like Xiaohongshu are capturing top-of-funnel consumer attention. By converting entertainment directly into purchases, they bypass traditional search-based e-commerce apps like JD.
  • Deflationary Price-War Traps: Persistent macroeconomic weakness in China has anchored consumer behavior to absolute low prices. Pinduoduo's aggressive merchant subsidy model continues to pressure JD's 1P margins, forcing JD to invest in defensive price-matching programs.
  • Local Instant Delivery Encroachment: Meituan and other instant-retail (Meituan Shangou) platforms are expanding from food delivery into electronics and cosmetics, offering 30-minute delivery from local physical stores. This directly challenges JD's "next-day" delivery value proposition for urgent purchases.

Thesis Falsification: 3 Quantitative Pre-Mortem Tripwires

An elite value investor must remain cold and objective. We will declare our investment thesis on JD.com fundamentally broken if any of the following operational tripwires are triggered over the next 12–18 months:

  1. JD Retail Gross Margin Compression: If JD Retail's gross margin falls below 17.0% (down from the current 18.5%), signaling that upstream supplier leverage has broken and JD is being forced to permanently absorb price-war costs.
  2. JD Logistics External Revenue Contraction: If JDL's external customer revenue growth slows to below 8.0% YoY for two consecutive quarters, proving that the logistics arm cannot successfully scale as a commercial enterprise and is reverting to a high-capex internal cost center.
  3. Active Customer Churn to Social Commerce: If JD's annual active customer count contracts by more than 3.0% annualized, indicating that the convenience and trust moat has failed to prevent structural customer migration to Douyin and other live-streaming platforms.

Section 3: Forensic Cash Flow, SBC Dilution & Owner Earnings Audit

To uncover the true economic reality of JD.com, Inc. (JD), we must look past promotional Non-GAAP metrics and conduct a rigorous, forensic audit of the company's cash generation. By stripping away working capital distortions, treating Stock-Based Compensation (SBC) as an unavoidable cash expense, and separating maintenance capital expenditures from growth-oriented investments, we derive the true "Buffett Owner Earnings" of this e-commerce and supply chain giant.

Forensic Insight on the FY 2025 Cash Flow Trough: In FY 2025, JD’s GAAP Operating Cash Flow experienced a severe, non-recurring contraction to RMB 18,991 million (~$2,675 million) from RMB 58,095 million (~$8,182 million) in FY 2024. This was not a breakdown of core profitability, but rather a temporary working capital distortion. As China rolled out its aggressive consumer trade-in subsidy programs for home appliances and electronics, JD—as the nation's dominant electronics retailer—fronted massive cash outflows to subsidize consumer purchases upfront, creating a temporary receivables drag before government remittances were processed. By Q2 2026, this working capital drag fully normalized, causing TTM Operating Cash Flow to surge back to RMB 51.1 billion (~$7,197 million).

SBC Dilution & Denominator Integrity Audit

Stock-Based Compensation is a real, non-negotiable economic expense. While Wall Street routinely adds back SBC to present inflated "Adjusted EBITDA" and "Non-GAAP Net Income" figures, we deduct 100% of SBC from our Owner Earnings. JD's SBC rose from RMB 2,999 million ($422 million) in FY 2024 to RMB 4,726 million ($666 million) in FY 2025, reflecting stock grants to retain key talent amid intense domestic competition. However, JD has aggressively neutralized this dilution through its massive share repurchase program. During the first six months of 2026, JD repurchased 69.9 million Class A ordinary shares (equivalent to 34.9 million ADSs) for $1.0 billion, representing approximately 2.5% of total ordinary shares outstanding. This programmatic buyback far outpaces SBC dilution, making JD a net "share cannibal" and compounding per-share intrinsic value for long-term owners.

This means JD receives cash from its retail customers over two weeks before it is contractually obligated to pay its suppliers, generating a massive $36.0 billion pool of interest-free float that perpetually funds its logistics network expansion without requiring dilutive equity or expensive debt issuance.

Munger's Balance Sheet Bridge & Margin of Safety

With a net cash position of RMB 129,750 million ($19,121 million), JD.com's net cash per share stands at RMB 46.08 ($6.79) per ordinary share, or RMB 92.15 ($13.58) per ADS (based on 2,816 million diluted ordinary shares outstanding). At a market price of ~$29.00 per ADS, the business is trading at an enterprise value that effectively values its core e-commerce and logistics operations at just ~$15.42 per ADS. This represents an extraordinary margin of safety where nearly 47% of the stock price is backed by cold, hard net cash.

Dilution vs. Cannibalization Analysis

JD.com's capital allocation strategy has shifted dramatically from aggressive capital reinvestment to massive shareholder returns. The company is actively shrinking its share count, making it a premier "share cannibal" in the global e-commerce landscape.

  • Programmatic Share Repurchases: Under the active $5.0 billion share repurchase program adopted in August 2024 (effective through August 2027), JD.com repurchased 69.9 million Class A ordinary shares (equivalent to 34.9 million ADSs) for a total consideration of US$1.0 billion during the first half of 2026. As of June 30, 2026, the remaining authorization under this program stands at US$1.0 billion.
  • SBC Dilution Sterilization: JD.com's programmatic buybacks have completely sterilized the dilutive impact of its employee stock-based compensation (SBC). While SBC runs at an annual rate of approximately RMB 16.25 billion, the scale of the buybacks has driven a massive net reduction in the share count.
  • True Net Annual Share Count Reduction:
    • Weighted Average Diluted Shares Outstanding in Q2 2025: 2,970 million ordinary shares.
    • Weighted Average Diluted Shares Outstanding in Q2 2026: 2,816 million ordinary shares.
    • True Net Annual Share Count Reduction: -5.19% per year.
    • Weighted Average Basic Shares Outstanding in Q2 2025: 2,841 million ordinary shares.
    • Weighted Average Basic Shares Outstanding in Q2 2026: 2,692 million ordinary shares.
    • True Net Annual Basic Share Count Reduction: -5.24% per year.

This aggressive cannibalization rate concentrates future owner earnings into fewer shares, compounding per-share intrinsic value at a rate that far outpaces top-line revenue growth.

Section 5: Warren Buffett Owner Earnings Intrinsic Valuation Matrix

Root valuation strictly in Warren Buffett's 1986 Owner Earnings methodology (GAAP OCF minus Maintenance CapEx minus 100% SBC). Valuation begins with 3 distinct, fundamental business narrative storylines covering 90–95% of probable future operating trajectories, followed by top-down unit economics modeling and discounted cash flow valuation.

3 Probable Business Storylines (The Narrative & Operational Paths)

📖 Storyline 1: Supply Chain Optimization & High-Margin Service Inflection

Under this operational path, JD.com prioritizes profitability and capital discipline over raw top-line GMV growth. Leveraging its proprietary supply chain and JD Logistics' highly automated warehousing network (Langzu-Tech), the company drives down fulfillment costs and expands operating efficiency. Management, led by CEO Sandy Xu and CFO Ian Shan, executes disciplined cost control, cutting marketing expenses (which dropped 24.8% year-over-year in Q2 2026) and narrowing losses in New Businesses (losses in food delivery cut by over 50% year-over-year). JD Retail returns to steady, moderate growth (5.0% revenue CAGR) while its operating margin expands toward its long-term high single-digit target (reaching 6.2%). High-margin marketplace and marketing (advertising) revenues grow at 8.3% year-over-year, improving the overall revenue mix. Exclusive partnerships, such as the exclusive e-commerce partnership with Costco in China and high-end brand launches (like the CHANEL beauty flagship), elevate the average user quality and lifetime value (LTV). Maintenance CapEx is tightly managed at 1.4% of total revenue, representing a disciplined compounding path where free cash flow is maximized and returned to shareholders via aggressive buybacks.

📖 Storyline 2: Omnichannel Ecosystem Integration & Global Expansion

Under this path, JD.com successfully executes its "World's Largest Operational Platform for the Physical World" strategy, driving top-line revenue at an 8.5% CAGR. The company integrates AI-powered supply chains (JoyAI LLM and JoyInside smart devices) to enhance user engagement and shopping frequency across both online and offline channels, including new JD MALL stores in high-tier cities. JD Food Delivery achieves a major operational turning point, leveraging cross-selling opportunities with the core supermarket category to drive high-frequency traffic. Joybuy successfully scales to over 30 European cities, establishing a robust cross-border supply chain corridor. JD Logistics continues its rapid expansion (growing at over 20% year-over-year), capturing third-party merchant volumes and deploying autonomous delivery fleets to optimize last-mile unit economics. Operating margins stabilize at 5.5% as increased reinvestment (Maintenance CapEx at 1.8% of revenue) offsets scale efficiencies, keeping cash flow generation robust while funding aggressive ecosystem growth.

📖 Storyline 3: Competitive Margin Compression & Macro-Driven Consumption Downshift

Under this defensive path, sluggish domestic consumption in China and intense price wars from low-cost platforms (such as Pinduoduo and Douyin) force JD.com into a defensive posture, resulting in a -1.0% revenue CAGR. To preserve its market share, the company is forced to maintain elevated marketing expenses and aggressive consumer subsidies (e.g., the RMB 10 billion subsidy program). Upstream component price inflation in consumer electronics and home appliances compresses gross margins by 180 basis points, while the high comparison base from previous trade-in programs weighs on product sales (which fell 11.8% in Q2 2026). Operating margins compress to 3.2%. New business investments (Joybuy and Jingxi) continue to burn cash without reaching self-sustaining scale, and JD Logistics faces price competition in third-party express delivery, leading to compressed group-level profitability. Underutilized logistics capacity and high fixed lease overhead drive maintenance capital requirements to 2.2% of revenue, forcing the company to run a defensive model with minimal top-line growth and severely compressed cash generation.
